newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ASMI issues profit warning, sees recovery in H2 97.
newsitem.headline: ASMI issues profit warning, sees recovery in H2 97.

text.p: Dutch semiconductor equipment maker ASM International NV (ASMI) announced plans for an offering of 4.1 million shares on Monday, but the news was overshadowed by an accompanying profit warning.

The company said that because of uncertainty in the market for semiconductors it expected earnings for the fourth quarter of 1996 and the first half of 1997 to show a substantial fall compared with year-earlier levels.
Despite this, ASMI said it planned to go ahead with plans to list its shares on the Amsterdam bourse later this month.
ASMI said the semiconductor industry had grown vigorously in the last two decades, driven by increasing use of personal computers and developments in telecommunications.
But it said its sales and earnings mirrored the investments of the industry, with periods of strong growth followed by stagnation during periods over overcapacity.
In the first half of 1996 ASMI's net income rose 41.5 percent to 27.5 million guilders ($15.90 million) but in the third quarter net income fell 71 percent to 6.8 million guilders.
Chief executive officer Arthur del Prado said ASMI expected the semiconductors market to recover in the second half of 1997.
"We are now somewhere at the bottom of the cycle, which we expect to pick up somewhere in the second half of 1997," he told reporters.

Del Prado declined to specify the extent of the expected drop in earnings and also declined to give a forecast beyond the first half of 1997, saying it was very difficult to pinpoint exactly when the industry would start to pick up again.
In the longer term Del Prado said ASMI expected to grow at a faster rate than the semiconductor industry as a whole.

The "front-end" semiconductors business of wafer-processing was growing at a rate of 17-20 percent per year, while the "back-end" business of assembly and encapsulation was growing at around 15 percent a year, he said.
AMSI, whose shares are currently traded on the Nasdaq exchange in the United States, said it would go ahead with plans to list its shares on the Amsterdam bourse from December 12.

To tie in with the Amsterdam listing ASMI is offering 1.5 million new shares to investors outside the United States while existing shareholders are selling an 2.6 million of the 31.5 million shares currently outstanding.
The price of the offering is expected to be set on December 12 by a book-building process under which investors indicate how many shares they want and the price they are willing to pay.
Merrill Lynch International is lead manager of the underwriting syndicate with ABN AMRO Rothschild and ING Barings acting as co-lead manager and co-manager respectively.
ASM International said the offering was intended to create additional liquidity in its shares for European investors.
Based on Nasdaq prices of November 27, the newly issued shares will raise some 26 million guilders for the company.
ASM International said it would use the proceeds to reduce its debts and for general corporate purposes. ($1=1.729 Guilder)
